content.title: How UCLA knocked off Texas to reach women's NCAA Tournament championship game
content.text: UCLA takes down TexasUCLA is headed to the national championship game for the first time in program history after beating Texas 51-44 in the women’s NCAA Tournament Final Four.The Bruins will face another SEC program, South Carolina, on Sunday for the title. UCLA center Lauren Betts had 16 points, 11 rebounds and three blocked shots, including a huge block on Madison Booker late in the game with the Bruins leading by three points.Share your thoughts on the game: live@theathletic.comSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLast time a Big Ten team won the title? Getty ImagesOne of the newest members of the Big Ten, UCLA will attempt to make history for the conference in the national championship on Sunday.The last Big Ten team to win it all? Purdue in 1999. The 20th century!Since then, Purdue, Michigan State and Iowa have reached the title game but lost in their respective appearances.On Sunday, it will be up to the Big Ten tournament champion to claim the conference's first title of this century.Readers' views on UCLA winBelow are some of your postgame reader thoughts on tonight’s UCLA and Texas semifinal.UCLA avenges regular-season loss to Texas Getty ImagesThe Final Four's Big Ten-SEC matchup was more familiar than the typical interconference matchup.Texas and UCLA played on Nov. 26, and the Longhorns won by double digits. At the time, Texas was No. 4 team in the nation, and UCLA ranked No. 3.To the surprise of very few, the game featured more points than the low-scoring Final Four rematch. Texas secured a 76-65 win with 26 points from Rori Harmon and 16 points from Madison Booker. Lauren Betts, the Bruins' leading scorer in the Final Four, posted just eight points in the teams' first meeting.UCLA's reward is a title game matchup against another SEC team, South Carolina, but the Bruins will face the Gamecocks for the first time this season.Bruins get a title shot UCLA will play for the national title for the first time in program history on Sunday against South Carolina. So how did the Bruins get past Texas to earn that matchup?Our Grace Raynor breaks it all down here.Betts' Final Four showing continues dominant tournament run Imagn ImagesUCLA's Lauren Betts was the most impactful and effective player on the court in the Bruins' matchup against the Texas Longhorns. Betts' heroics are nothing new. Here's how she has performed through this year's NCAA Tournament:First round against California Baptist: 22 points, 9-15 FG, 10 rebounds, 1 blockSecond round against Oklahoma State: 35 points, 15-19 FG, 9 rebounds, 1 blockSweet 16 against Minnesota: 16 points, 7-9 FG, 5 rebounds, 5 blocksElite Eight against Duke: 23 points, 9-14 FG, 10 rebounds, 5 blocksFinal Four against Texas: 16 points, 7-10 FG, 11 rebounds, 3 blocksSKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementSouth Carolina-UCLA history Getty ImagesSouth Carolina and UCLA have faced off five times in their history, with South Carolina winning four times.2024-25: UCLA 77-622022-23: South Carolina 59-432022-23: South Carolina 73-642016-17: South Carolina 66-572015-16: South Carolina 65-68When is the title game? Getty ImagesSunday's national title game between UCLA and South Carolina will tip off at 3:30 p.m. ET. UCLA wins despite 23 turnovers Getty ImagesUCLA earned its spot in the national championship in a 51-44 win over Texas, but one aspect the Bruins will look to clean up on Sunday is protecting the basketball.The Bruins committed 23 turnovers — 11 more than Texas committed — and that carelessness allowed the Longhorns to turn a game UCLA almost led wire-to-wire into a nail-biter late. Nineteen of those 23 turnovers came from the Bruins' starters, and six came in the final quarter with UCLA attempting to close the game out.UCLA benefited from the Longhorns failing to take full advantage of those turnovers (Texas turned those turnovers into 15 points), and the Bruins can't count on South Carolina also failing to capitalize.Staley on facing UCLA Getty ImagesDawn Staley to Scott Van Pelt just now on "SportsCenter" on facing UCLA: 💬 “It’s the same kind of approach, we’ll probably be the underdogs in the next game. Same approach, once you get to this point in the season, you’re going to do whatever is necessary in order for us to win, continue to belief, continue to lock in, continue to execute.”Close on limiting Booker Getty ImagesMadison Booker finished 3-of-23 from the floor tonight.Here is UCLA coach Cori Close on limiting the Texas star: 💬 “It was the focus of our group to just make her catches more uncomfortable. … We wanted her catches to happen at 17 (instead of 12) feet. … Madison Booker is an incredible player, I’ve watched her with USA Basketball and obviously her career at Texas.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFinal stats Getty ImagesFG:Texas: 20-of-65UCLA: 18-of-443FG:Texas: 2-of-9UCLA: 4-of-13Rebounds: Texas: 36UCLA: 37Assists:Texas: 11UCLA: 13Steals:Texas: 14UCLA: 5Turnovers:Texas: 12UCLA: 23Points in the paint: Texas: 24UCLA: 24Largest lead: Texas: 2UCLA: 13UCLA-Texas heated up in final quarter Getty ImagesAt the start of the third quarter, UCLA coach Cori Close apologized to fans watching the UCLA-Texas semifinal matchup for its terrible shooting efficiency and "rugby match" physicality.But fans and viewers were rewarded for their patience in a final quarter that saw Texas nearly complete its rally from a 13-point deficit and cut UCLA's lead to a possession in the final minutes. UCLA ultimately won 51-44, and maybe more impressively considering the flow of the game to that point, it exceeded 50 points.Here's how the combined quarter point totals compared:First quarter: 20 pointsSecond quarter: 17 pointsThird quarter: 22 pointsFourth quarter: 36 pointsUCLA one win away Getty ImagesUCLA achieved program history. It’s the first time the Bruins women’s basketball program advances to the national title game.Previously, UCLA was 0-1 in the women’s Final Four. Now 1-1 after avenging last year’s loss to UConn in the semis. The Bruins are one win away from a maiden national championship. Final scoring leaders Getty ImagesBelow are the final scoring leaders for Texas and UCLA:Texas: Kyla Oldacre (11 points, 5-of-10 FG)UCLA: Lauren Betts (16 points, 7-of-10 FG)Cori Close: 'We stayed connected' Getty ImagesUCLA coach Cori Close admitted after the game that it wasn’t the prettiest basketball, but she was proud of her players for finding a way to grind out the win.💬 “It wasn’t the sport I thought I was coaching. It was more rugby than it was basketball.”💬 “There were ups and downs, but I thought we stayed connected, and I thought we were pretty darn tough on the defensive end so we can weather the storm on the defensive end.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementLauren Betts: 'I wanted to win this for my team' Getty ImagesAfter the game, Lauren Betts spoke about finally advancing to the national championship and, of course, that epic block. 💬 “I just wanted to win it so bad for this team. We work so hard, it’s just execution. When you work so hard in practice and … you’re consistent every day, great things happen."On the block: 💬 “My instincts. Just playing defense, protecting the basket. It’s what I do, helping my team out. We just earned another day with each other, and I’m so happy. … This group is amazing, and I love my team so much.”Betts turns back to her team and yells, “We’re playing in the national championship!”Double-double for BettsIt’s no secret that this was an ugly basketball game. But Lauren Betts once again found a way to lead her team to victory with a gutsy effort.Betts recorded a double-double with 16 points and 11 rebounds. She also made the critical block in the dying seconds with UCLA up three, en route to victory. She is playing for her first national title. What a career she’s had with the Bruins. National title game setA fascinating women’s national championship game awaits.UCLA versus South Carolina. The Bruins trying to win their first national title in program history. South Carolina going for its fourth. A lot on the line in Phoenix on Sunday. UCLA defeats Texas to advance to title game Getty ImagesFINAL – UCLA 51, Texas 44UCLA is headed to its first national championship game!Lauren Betts tallied 16 points and 11 rebounds, but the game's iconic play is her resounding block in the final minute that both denied Madison Booker's reverse layup attempt and directed the ball back to the Bruins. What a defensive effort from UCLA and what poise in the final moments.The Bruins will play the South Carolina Gamecocks on Sunday for the title.Vic Schaefer applauds Harmon as she comes off the court and is giving her a long talk now. They both smile at each other and exchange a long hug before shaking hands with UCLA.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementA sad goodbye for HarmonYou can start to see the emotions on Rori Harmon's face as she processes the end of her college career. Tough way to go out, even if Texas bettered its performance from last year's Final Four.Q4 3.1 – UCLA 49, Texas 44Oh no.What a disastrous possession for Texas. Madison Booker slips while driving to the basket, and Kyla Oldacre misses a baseline jumper that ricochets off the backboard.Rice hits clutch free throws Getty ImagesQ4 0:13 – UCLA 49, Texas 44Kiki Rice makes both of her free-throw attempts to boost the UCLA lead up to two possessions. 13 seconds left, and Texas is running out of time.Q4 0:14 – UCLA 47, Texas 44After a quick Texas foul on the inbounds play, Texas coach Vic Schaefer calls a timeout to coordinate the Longhorns’ defense. One job for UCLA: Do not turn the ball over.Feels like the obvious, but after UConn-Duke on the men's side, we know it’s not always.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA calls its final timeout Getty ImagesLast timeout for UCLA, which has had to use three in the last 10 minutes to avoid five-second inbounding violations.HUGE block from Lauren Betts.UCLA being smart here to not shoot the ball. Hold on to it.Betts with the block! Imagn ImagesQ4 0:18 – UCLA 47, Texas 44Madison Booker takes a defensive rebound coast to coast but is denied on her reverse layup attempt by, who else, Lauren Betts. What a swat by Betts!We're 18 seconds away from the end of regulation, and UCLA has just used its last timeout.Rori Harmon picks off Kiki Rice’s dribble and it leads to a Jordan Lee bucket. Longhorns are making things happen after being down 13.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA lead down to 3 points Getty ImagesQ4 0:55 – UCLA 47, Texas 44Texas has cut its deficit to three points!!Jordan Lee spins in the post and banks in the layup to cut the UCLA lead to 47-44. UCLA calls timeout after surrendering seven straight points.It seemed like the UCLA bench was up in arms because Dugalic went too early, but you could clearly hear Cori Close yell "that's a f***in foul" when the play ended.The broadcast just showed some impressive Lauren Betts numbers: in her time at UCLA, she’s averaging 17 ppg, shooting 61 percent. But in the NCAA Tournament, she averages 22 on 68 percent. Made for the moment, if you will.Betts' double-double powers UCLA to late advantage Getty ImagesQ4 2:18 – UCLA 47, Texas 40Lauren Betts beats an expiring clock and nails a post shot to interrupt the Texas run. Betts is shining on the Final Four stage: 16 points on efficient 7-10 shooting, 10 rebounds and two blocks. And while less quantifiable, her defense on Madison Booker has swung this game and disrupted the Texas offense.UCLA has moved past the tying shoes to waste time tactic, instead Kneepkens just walked off the court painfully slowly before the bench signaled for an appeal.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCori Close is not happy with that call on Dugalic. "NO WAY" she screams. "NO WAY."Betts-Kneepkens connection culminates in another 3-pointerUCLA loves the inside out. Lauren Betts to Gianna Kneepkens and UCLA takes its largest lead of the night, up 45-32 with four minutes on the clockTexas cuts into UCLA's leadQ4 3:35 – UCLA 45, Texas 37We still have 3:39 to go in the fourth quarter, but it’s already the most high-scoring quarter of the game. It's not a high bar.Jordan Lee and Madison Booker are knocking down shots for the Longhorns, who trim a UCLA lead that reached a game-high 13 points down to eight.Q4 5:50 – UCLA 42, Texas 30Texas faces a 12-point deficit with just under six minutes to go ... in a game it has not eclipsed that total in any of the prior three quarters. A full rally seems unlikely, given the Longhorns have made one 3-pointer tonight and are still struggling with turnovers. The defense is showing out, but this would be an agonizing way for the season to end.Oh, how I long for a team that can shoot 40 percent from the field.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBooker returns to the court Getty ImagesQ4 8:30 – UCLA 38, Texas 28Texas is looking for a spark in its timeout. Is Madison Booker the answer?No. 35 has missed her last 15 field-goal attempts, but she re-enters the game after the timeout.A 10-point lead feels somewhat insurmountable in this 1930s-era game.UCLA extends lead to 10 points Getty ImagesQ4 8:30 – UCLA 38, Texas 28Lauren Betts corrals a lob and redirects the ball out to the perimeter, where Kiki Rice drains the 3-pointer. On the next possession, Gabriela Jaquez turns a UCLA steal into a basket in transition.The UCLA lead is back up to 10 points, and Texas calls a timeout.Close on low-scoring semifinal: 'I feel bad for the fans' Getty ImagesUCLA coach Cori Close on the ESPN broadcast:💬 "It’s a darn rugby match. … It’s going to come down to toughness. I feel bad for the fans. 31-28, it’s an ugly basketball game.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRori Harmon attempts the fadeaway at the buzzer, but it’s long and Lauren Betts grabs her 11th board of the night (she’s at her 15th double double of the season).Second half of UCLA-Texas still a slugfest Getty ImagesQ3 0.0 – UCLA 31, Texas 28Justice Carlton’s 7-0 run rallied the Longhorns back into this one, but UCLA maintains the lead going into the final quarter.Though it was the first quarter in this game in which both teams scored in double digits, that third quarter was just brutal to watch. Texas made 5-of-16 field goals, while UCLA hit 4-of-13. Will either team get to 40 points??Time for a Texas press? Getty ImagesHere comes Texas. The Longhorns are within one point. Agree with Sabreena: Bring on the Texas press. It's clearly working on a night when offense is already hard to come by.Charlisse Leger-Walker is called for a foul as UCLA once again can't break Texas' press, and she's telling the official that Harmon was grabbing her jersey. This fourth quarter is bound to be chippy with how both teams feel about the officiating.I maintain that Texas should be pressing full court more often. Admittedly, the Longhorns have to make shots for that to happen, but it's been going very well for them whenever they do.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCarlton ignites the Texas offenseQ3 0:53 – UCLA 29, Texas 26Coming off a four-minute scoreless stretch, Texas is making a run to cut down its deficit at the end of a low-scoring third quarter. Justice Carlton makes a contested layup and draws contact, then converts the free throw for her fifth-straight point. Despite Texas shooting 4-of-13 from the field in this quarter, we’re back to a one-possession game. Texas living up to its feisty reputation Getty ImagesHolly Rowe said Cori Close showed the Bruins clips from the Texas-Michigan game to show how feisty and aggressive the Longhorns are going to be, putting a “chip on their shoulder” heading into tonight.Just about every number on my screen feels like a typo. What is happening?!While most eyes will go to Madison Booker’s 1-of-14 line, at the same time, three Texas starters haven’t scored a bucket. Yet the Longhorns are down just five points in the third quarter. Tells you about this game.Q3 3:00 – UCLA 28, Texas 21Lauren Betts is up to 10 points after another basket down low.Betts is commanding the Texas define’s attention, and her last layup on a pick and roll was all too easy. The center also has nine rebounds and two blocks.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisement Can't say this enough about the UCLA turnovers: The Bruins are so lucky most of them are dead balls, including that last one that could have been a steal but was ruled a held ball. Getty ImagesThat’s Gabriela Jaquez for you. Came out of absolutely nowhere for the board and put back.On a team with Betts and Rice dominating most of the headlines, Jaquez probably doesn't get enough credit. She is everywhere crashing the boards, hustling for loose balls, etc. Q3 7:19 – UCLA 22, Texas 19Officials rule no excessive contact from Madison Booker, so no flagrant foul.Lauren Betts just fell hard on the floor face first. She gets up on her own (not sure why none of the UCLA trainers went to help her) and is holding her head but looks to be OK.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementBetts foul under review for contact to the head Getty ImagesScary moment here as Lauren Betts falls to the floor after a collision with Madison Booker. She got up on her own, but it sounded pretty loud. The officials are reviewing the play for contact to the head.Scary foul from BookerQ3 7:19 – UCLA 22, Texas 19Yikes! Madison Booker chases an offensive rebound and collides with UCLA's Lauren Betts. Both players looked shaken up by the play.Booker gets called for a foul, and the officials are reviewing the play for a potential upgrade.It’s been a rough night for Booker, who made a shot in the first minute of the game and has missed her 13 shots since. Getty ImagesQ3 7:41 – UCLA 22, Texas 19Texas coach Vic Schaefer appeals an out-of-bounds call, sending the game to a media timeout.The third quarter has looked much like the first – strong defensive play, less-than-ideal shooting. UCLA opened the quarter in promising fashion when Kiki Rice turned an offensive rebound into a basket, but it’s been the only third-quarter make for the Bruins so far.UCLA band and practice players chanting "we want fries!" after Oldacre's first missed free throw, because the fans get free fries in Pauley Pavilion in an opponent misses the pair.Lauren Betts needs a big second half Lauren Betts continues to be a force. She had six first-half points on 3-of-5 shooting from the floor. Betts also added four rebounds. Betts is the only UCLA starter to not have a turnover. She will be key for the Bruins to build their lead. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA-Texas back for second half Getty ImagesQ3 10:00 – UCLA 20, Texas 17We have 20 minutes to determine which team will play South Carolina for the national championship!UCLA and Texas are back to compete to for the last championship game spot and (hopefully) score more points than in the first half.First-half readers' viewsHere are some readers' thoughts on a low-scoring first half between Texas and UCLA.A lot share a similar sentiment that more offense is desired. Harmon guiding Texas Getty ImagesRori Harmon is the reason why Texas is in this game. She scored eight points on 4-of-6 shooting from the floor.Harmon also led the team in rebounds with four. Her stellar play will need to continue in the second half. Turnovers a common theme in UCLA-Texas games Getty ImagesUCLA's season-high in turnovers was 20 against Texas in the Bruins' lone loss in November. UCLA already is at 12 today, but the Longhorns have managed only eight points off the miscues.Tough half for Booker Getty ImagesMadison Booker is not having a great game. She is 1-of-12 from the field (8 percent).It’s a part of a tough first-half shooting performance for Texas, currently at 25 percent from the field and 17 percent from 3.These numbers will need to improve if Texas wants to win this game. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFirst-half leading scorers Imagn ImagesBelow are your first half scoring leaders in the Texas and UCLA game: Texas: Rori Harmon (8 points, 4-of-6 FG)UCLA: Gianna Kneepkens (7 points, 3-of-8 FG)First-half stats Getty ImagesFG:Texas: 8-of-32UCLA: 9-of-243FG:Texas: 1-of-6UCLA: 2-of-8Rebounds:Texas: 18UCLA: 21Assists:Texas: 5UCLA: 7Steals:Texas: 8UCLA: 2Turnovers:Texas: 5UCLA: 12Points in the paint: Texas: 6UCLA: 10Largest lead: Texas: 2UCLA: 10Just 37 combined points in first half Getty ImagesWe have a very low-scoring game in Phoenix. UCLA leads Texas 20-17 at the half, after the Bruins put up just six points in the second quarter; Longhorns had 11.Texas defense shines in low-scoring first halfThis is, if anything a show of how good Texas' defense is that its best player is 1-12 from the floor and yet this score is 20-17 at halftime. They haven't let UCLA out of their grasp.After a 26-24 first half in Game 1, we're at 20-17 in Game 2. Maybe these rims are the ones that are a little off.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementObviously, Texas wants (and needs) to get Booker going, but for the Longhorns to still be within three with her looking a little off bodes well for Schaefer's team, no?Madison Booker is now 1-for-12 from the field.We're once again more than eight minutes into the period before the first foul is called.UCLA leads by 1 possession at halftime Getty ImagesHALF – UCLA 20, Texas 17After UCLA’s defense held Texas to six points in the first quarter, the Longhorns returned the favor by limiting the Bruins to six points in the second.UCLA still holds its first-quarter lead, but the Bruins hit 3-of-11 field-goal attempts and turned the ball over seven times in an ugly offensive quarter.Rori Harmon leads all scorers with eight points, while UCLA’s Lauren Betts has six points, four rebounds and a block. Harmon leading Longhorns through low-scoring gameQ2 1:17 – UCLA 20, Texas 17Rori Harmon is picking up the slack for Texas with stars Madison Booker and Jordan Lee struggling on offense.Harmon has scored six of her eight points in the second quarter, including the last layup on a steal and coast-to-coast basket. Even the misses (a mid-ranger that clanked off the rim after a killer crossover) look smooth.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementI'm surprised Texas isn't full-court pressing on every make.After coming out hot, UCLA has allowed Texas to climb back to 18-15. Good news, though? Madison Booker is 1 for 11.Booker is in the type of straitjacket South Carolina's Bree Hall used to put her in.Betts is dominating for UCLA Getty ImagesEasy solution to UCLA's offensive woes? Just get Betts the ball, whether in the paint or not. She can get to work.Texas rallies after timeoutQ2 4:45 – UCLA 18, Texas 15Texas gets exactly what it was looking for out of the timeout. Rori Harmon is on point with her bounce pass to Kyla Oldacre for an easy layup. On the next possession, it's Harmon's turn for a mid-range jumper from the free-throw line. Lauren Betts answers back with a post bucket, but Aaliyah Crump swishes a 3-pointer off an offensive rebound to close the Texas deficit to three points.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementKyla Oldacre has the size to meaningfully affect Betts. Her length is getting in Betts' way, and she even scored in isolation on the UCLA center. But Booker is off to an atrocious start, 1-of-9 from the field.Gianna Kneepkens is doing a great job on Madison Booker.So much contact being allowed in this game, it looked like Charlisse Leger-Walker just cleared out Harmon, and there was no call.Schaefer assesses Longhorns' slow startTexas coach Vic Schaefer on what’s going wrong so far: 💬 “They’re doing as much as we’re doing to ourselves. … We’re taking some really bad shots. We’re not attacking the rim. … I don’t think it’s them as much as us.”UCLA leads by 8 after first quarterEND Q1: UCLA 14, Texas 6 (season low for Longhorns)Madison Booker and Rori Harmon have been limited to 2 each. Lauren Betts, Gianna Kneepkens, Gabriela Jaquez and Angela Dugalic are all on the board for UCLA. Some key numbers:Texas shooting 21 percent, UCLA 46Bruins winning the board battle 11-7UCLA has 2 more turnovers than Texas, but has 6 points in the paint to Texas’ 2.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA holds Texas to 6 points in first quarter Q1 0.0 – UCLA 14, Texas 6The first quarter was all UCLA. Texas couldn’t get its offense going early, and UCLA took full advantage of a Texas scoring drought of almost five minutes. Just six points in that quarter!For UCLA, Gianna Kneepkens and Lauren Betts combine for nine of the Bruins' 14 points. UCLA also owns an 11-7 advantage in rebounding.Kiki Rice pretty clearly got away with hitting Madison Booker in the face trying to clear some space on offense, and it led to UCLA's first live-ball turnover, but the Bruins got back on defense quickly. Imagn ImagesThree turnovers for UCLA so far, but they're all dead-ball. Not letting Texas get going in transition.Biggest Texas deficit in nearly two months Imagn ImagesPer the broadcast, Texas’ 14-4 deficit is its largest not only of the tournament, but since Feb. 12 at Vanderbilt. Since then, the Longhorns have won 12 games consecutively by about 26.5 points.UCLA enjoys excellent start Getty ImagesGonna repeat myself here: This is exactly what the Bruins wanted and needed. A hot start. They’re moving the ball and shooting 46 percent from the field, 50 percent from deep with 2 minutes to play. All the while, Texas is just 2 of 9 from the field and hasn’t converted from beyond the arc.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementUCLA is off to a fast start with a 10-point lead here in the first quarter. Today it's Kneepkens who has the hot hand with five points already.Read more on Dugalić's unique storyStrong fist pump from Angela Dugalić after she hit Jaquez on that baseline cut. If you want to learn more about UCLA's sixth player...Texas offense struggles to open Final Four matchupQ1 2:08 – UCLA 14, Texas 4Texas faces its first double-digit deficit of the NCAA tournament, and the Longhorns’ cold offense is a major reason why.Texas stars Jordan Lee and Madison Booker have combined to make just one of their first seven shots from the field, and the Longhorns have yet to record an offensive rebound.After the Texas scoring drought extends to more than four minutes, coach Vic Schaefer calls timeout.This is Texas’ largest deficit of the tournament
